messages:
maya: quick ask — can someone run a focused latency + throughput scan for a new model (peridot-6b v1) on test-3 dedicated pool? suspect p95 regression vs sapphire-6b on short prompts. targets: seq=256, batches=1,4,8, variants=fp16 and q4_0. please include cold vs warm (kv cache warmup 5 requests) and GPU util / kernel breakdown. need a short summary + CSV by EOD PST. tagging @arjun @jon :eyes:

arjun: on it. i'll queue on test-3. do you want exact prompt sampling or synthetic tokens? also confirm route (dedicated-us-west.test3).

jon: i can run synthetics now and a small sample with real prompts later. what qps should i use for throughput sweep?

maya: use synthetic first: 1 qps up to 50 qps ramp for throughput profile. for latency, single-request steady state and then 10qps sanity. route: dedicated-us-west.test3.redwood.internal. model path: gs://models/peridot-6b/v1. baseline: sapphire-6b:v3. here's the perf-run command we usually use:

```
perf-run --model gs://models/peridot-6b/v1 \n         --variant fp16,q4_0 \n         --seq 256 \n         --batches 1,4,8 \n         --latency --throughput \n         --cold-warm 5 \n         --out /tmp/peridot_run.json
```

maya: include a small note if you see kv-evictions or outlier evict patterns. claire suggested capping kv cache to 1GB for parity with baseline.

perf-bot: job queued (id=job-97421). estimated runtime ~45m. logs will be here: https://perf-logs/redwood/job-97421

jon: quick update — kicked off fp16 cold run batch=1. first numbers (cold): peridot fp16 p50=88ms p95=210ms, sapphire baseline fp16 p50=82ms p95=190ms. stack shows slightly higher kernel time on matmul. uploading raw to /tmp and will push to sheet.

claire: can you also capture max RSS and nvtop snapshot? we need to rule out memory thrash. i'll keep kv cache capped to 1GB for both runs.

jon: nvtop + nsys traces are on the run. GPU util peaked 78% on peridot (fp16, batch1 cold). nsys shows a 12% higher matmul time vs baseline. no OOMs.

arjun: thanks — after the cold run please do a warm run (send 5 warmup requests, then measure). also include one q4_0 run at batch=1 to compare quantization impact.

jon: warm run results: peridot fp16 p50=72ms p95=140ms; sapphire p50=68ms p95=128ms. q4_0 peridot p95=165ms (warm). throughput sweep summary: batch1 steady-state qps ~85 req/s p95 ~160ms, batch4 ~320 req/s p95 ~250ms. uploading CSV + short notes to sheet: https://goose.example/sheets/perf-peridot-6b (private).

tim: heads-up — could be a kernel selection issue on peridot's fused attention. can we capture kernel names/times from the nsys report?

jon: yes, attaching top kernels: 
- matmul_gemm_fp16 (42%)
- flash_attn_fwd (26%)
- layernorm (8%)
Full breakdown linked in sheet and raw nsys tarball on perf-logs.

maya: this is super helpful, thanks team. next steps: arjun, can you try a short compile with alternative kernel set (force_always_flash_attn=true) and rerun the warm fp16 batch1 to see delta? if that improves p95, we'll consider a default kernel override for peridot.

arjun: will try a quick compile and report back in ~30m.

maya: also cc'ing product in a follow-up, but for now :thumbsup: great quick turnaround. i'll synthesize notes for the rollout doc.

jon: filed short summary in sheet and marked regression flag. will keep the raw artifacts in perf-logs/job-97421 and tag the PR with results.

perf-bot: job completed (id=job-97421). artifacts: https://perf-logs/redwood/job-97421/artifacts.tar.gz

maya: closing the loop — thanks everyone. we have enough to justify a kernel experiment before any canary. i'll post follow-up once arjun's compile run completes.
